Humble & wholesome vegan restaurant
Sep 2019 • Solo
I visited here for lunch on my last day in Hanoi and I’m very glad that I did. I was the only tourist in the restaurant and the atmosphere was cosy and welcoming. Service was efficient without being fussy and the restaurant is clean. This is a Buddhist establishment so you can be reassured that the food is prepared correctly without animal products. There’s plenty to choose from and the prices are very reasonable. I chose one of the set menu options which cost less than 70.000VND (absolute bargain). 

The menu is diverse and organised in set recommendations (a collection of courses) and individual dishes. There is a lot of ‘mock meat’ as well as tofu on the menu, so those who need gluten free will need to be careful. I would definitely recommend this restaurant for authentic Vietnamese vegetarian food in a clean environment - just don’t be afraid to follow the long alleyway from the road to find it! I visited at 12.00 which was a good time for a buzzy atmosphere without being crowded. If I lived in Hanoi I would come here at least once a month. Try it!

Com Yay
Aug 2019 • Couples
So this restaurant is a little bit hidden and the easiest way to spot it is the neon lit sign on Tran Hung Dao. The opening hours are off, we went at 4:00 and it wasn’t open and we were told we should come back at 5:00. We are so glad we did, we had a set meal for 85kVND per person so less than £3.50, and what an awesome meal it was. Staff were pleasant and the food just tasted amazing. Also the portions were huge definitely would recommend for any vegetarian in Hanoi. Don’t be put off when they put pork, it means tofu made to look at taste like pork. We asked to double check the look is so convincing but poking it it’s obviously tofu! Overall amazing meal and will be going again before we leave ♥️

Great find
Jan 2019 • Couples
This is tucked away amongst embassies on Tran Hung Dao st. Really pleased we found it. The menu explains that Buddhists have long prepared food that looks like meat, to make their carnivorous guests feel more at home. So there is fake chicken, beef, fish as well as more traditional vegetarian dishes. I chose 'beef' and pineapple which was lovely, (looked but didn't taste like beef), as was my wife's noodle dish and the spring rolls and fried tofu starters. Very extensive and creative menu, including things like 'snail and banana' . You can have beer, but there's no wine. Staff were ok, food was very quickly cooked, fresh and very tasty. Excellent veggie food but felt genuinely Vietnamese.
